experiments.hypothesis: Blog readers who reach the 2nd H2 of a long-form physics post are at a natural mid-scroll section break and have already invested ~3 minutes of reading attention. The current end-of-post CTA fires only after they finish — by which point they are mentally exiting. Placing a pull-quote-style simulator CTA after the 2nd H2 (with copy + href identical to the end-of-post card so placement is the only variable) should lift simulator-runs / blog-post-visitor without cannibalising the end-of-post CTA, because mid-scroll click-throughs come from a reader cohort that would otherwise have bounced before the article end.

experiments.variant_b: End-of-post CTA + pull-quote-style inline CTA after 2nd H2 (mid-scroll)

experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/blog-post-visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND end-of-post CTA absolute CTR does not drop >25% (we want net new clicks, not redistributed clicks — if mid-scroll cannibalises end-of-post entirely we have not actually lifted the page). Roll back if scroll_depth_pct drops >10% (inline CTA causing premature exits) or post_dwell_time_s drops >15% (CTA disrupting reading flow). No decision before 200 samples per arm. If B wins, replicate the pattern across the other 7 blog posts in a follow-up rollout (one post at a time so each replication is its own micro-validation, not a blanket assumption).

experiments.element: Pro tier tag-line (the descriptor under the price)
experiments.hypothesis: Visitors who reach /pricing after running a free simulation already know they want more capability — what they are evaluating is 'will Pro tell me something I can act on?' The current Pro tag line 'Everything you need to go faster' is aspirational but non-specific; it could describe any racing product. Variant B replaces it with a line that names the three specific analytical outputs unique to Pro (unlimited sims, ROI per part, build optimizer) and frames them as a decision tool ('know what each mod does before you buy it'). If specificity reduces the 'is this worth ₹499?' hesitation, pro_checkout_init / pricing_visitor should rise.

experiments.element: end-of-grid simulator CTA card on the blog index
experiments.hypothesis: The blog index renders 22 post cards and ends. Visitors who scroll the full grid are high-intent (they came to learn drag racing physics) but the page offers no terminal action — they either click a post or bounce. Adding a grid-aligned simulator CTA card after the last post should capture the cohort of visitors who finished scanning the list without finding a post that grabbed them, converting otherwise-bounced traffic into /simulator runs. Placement-only test: copy + href are fixed across arms so we are not confounding presence with messaging.
experiments.variant_a: No terminal CTA — post grid ends, footer follows (existing control)
experiments.variant_b: End-of-grid CTA card pinned below the post grid: 'Stop reading. Run the numbers on your bike.' → /simulator

experiments.hypothesis: First-time visitors arriving at /login (especially via the /signup → /login?signup=1 redirect, and from /pricing or blog CTAs) hesitate at the form because the submit button says 'Send sign-in link' — copy that describes the email-delivery mechanism rather than the outcome the visitor wants ('start using the product, free, with no password'). For returning users the mechanism wording is fine; for first-time-signup intent it raises the perceived friction ('do I need an account first? is this a sign-in for people who already signed up somewhere else?'). Variant B replaces the button with 'Start free · email me the link' — names the outcome (start free), embeds the zero-friction promise on the click target itself, and retains the mechanism noun ('link') so the action remains unambiguous. If the value-forward CTA reduces the moment-of-click hesitation, magic-link-request submits per /login visitor should rise.
experiments.variant_b: Start free · email me the link

EXP-001 on landing-hero, EXP-002+EXP-005 on /pricing, EXP-003 on /simulator, EXP-004 on /blog/the-physics-of-a-perfect-launch, EXP-006 on /blog — no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if magic_link_requests/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND magic_link_verification_completion_rate does not drop >5% (we want intent-to-start-using, not inflated submit clicks from visitors who never click through the email — if verification rate collapses, B is recruiting low-quality intent and should be rolled back). Roll back if login_page_bounce_rate rises >10% (button copy reads spammy / scammy) or returning_user_friction_signal increases (e.g. existing-user reports finding the page confusing — surfaced via support tickets, not analytics). If B wins, evaluate the segmented-default follow-up (auto-B for ?signup=1 traffic, control for direct /login traffic) as a separate experiment — do not bundle the two changes.

experiments.hypothesis: Visitors who reach the bottom of /features have read 6 feature blocks and are evaluating 'is this real, and what will actually happen if I click?' The current CTA 'Try it free' with subhead 'Free in the browser. No account required to start.' restates the free-ness twice but never names the concrete first-run outcome. Variant B replaces the button with 'Run a sim — 15 seconds, no signup' and the subhead with 'Pick a bike, hit go. Real physics in your browser — no install, no account.' — both name the action ('run a sim'), the time cost ('15 seconds'), and the absence of friction ('no signup', 'no install') on the click target itself. If grounding the next click in a time-bound, action-specific promise reduces drop-off vs the generic free-ness framing, simulator-runs / features-page-visitor should rise. Distinct from EXP-001 (landing-hero, cold visitor) — this is a mid-funnel feature-reader cohort with higher intent but also higher 'is this real?' skepticism.

If B wins, evaluate replicating the time-bound + action-specific pattern on the landing-page hero (a follow-up to EXP-001, possibly as a 3-way test if EXP-001 has resolved by then) as a SEPARATE experiment — do not bundle. experiments.element: inline 'Run sim' pill on each BikeCard in the catalog grid
experiments.hypothesis: Visitors who land on /bikes are in a 'browse / lookup' mode — they scroll the 754-bike grid (40 per page, paginated), find their bike, and click into the detail page to read specs. The current BikeCard has exactly one action: a Link wrapping the whole card that navigates to /bikes/<id>. The simulator is mentioned only in a prose sentence inside the header subtitle ('open the quarter-mile calculator'), which most grid-scanners never read. This funnels nearly all catalog traffic into the detail page, not the simulator — even though every grid visitor implicitly has the question 'what does this bike actually run?' which is what the simulator answers. Variant B adds a small, secondary 'Run sim' pill in the bottom-right corner of each card, absolutely positioned outside the parent Link so it can navigate to /simulator independently. The detail-page Link remains the dominant card action (same hover area, same group-hover styling); the pill is a visual minority. Hypothesis: an inline catalog → simulator affordance, even a small one, will lift simulator-runs/bikes-visitor without cannibalising the detail-page CTR (the pill is small and offset; the card body still links to the detail page). Distinct from EXP-001 (landing-hero, cold visitor) and EXP-008 (features-page bottom CTA, evaluation mid-funnel) — this is a high-intent catalog-browsing cohort whose primary friction is awareness, not motivation. /bikes had zero live experiments prior to this.
experiments.variant_a: control: BikeCard has no inline simulator CTA; entire card links to /bikes/<id> only
experiments.variant_b: BikeCard gains a small 'Run sim' pill in the bottom-right corner linking to /simulator (event.stopPropagation on click so the parent Link doesn't fire); pill styling matches brand-orange catalog accent (border + 10% fill, monospace uppercase 10px, Zap icon), small enough to read as a secondary action rather than competing with the dominant card-body link
experiments.implementation_notes: useSearchParams() lives inside VariantPillInner in web/app/bikes/BikeCardCta.js, wrapped in <Suspense fallback={null}> per the App-Router static-prerender / CSR-bailout rule documented in CLAUDE.md. The Suspense fallback is null, meaning the SSR/SSG output for both arms is byte-identical to the pre-EXP-009 page — zero layout shift, zero hydration mismatch, zero SEO drift on the control. BikeCard structure was minimally restructured: outer <Link> wrapping the entire card is unchanged (preserves the dominant action + SEO link graph); a sibling <div className='absolute bottom-3 right-3'> hosts the BikeCardCta component so we never nest <a> tags (invalid HTML). On variant A, BikeCardCta renders null and the absolutely-positioned div is empty (no visual change vs control). On variant B, the pill links to /simulator with onClick={e=>e.stopPropagation()} so the parent <Link> click handler doesn't navigate to /bikes/<id>. data-exp='EXP-009' on the wrapper div AND data-variant + data-cta + data-bike-id on the pill itself, so click-attribution survives if either layer of analytics misfires. No page conflict with EXP-001..008 — /bikes had no live experiments. The pill links to /simulator without a ?bike=<id> query param because the simulator does not currently honour a bike deeplink and EXP-003 owns the simulator's own variant flag; bundling a deeplink would confound EXP-009 with a separate feature (multi-variable test, against guidance).
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/bikes-visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND bikes_to_detail_page_ctr does not drop >10% (we want incremental simulator traffic, not cannibalised detail-page traffic — if detail CTR collapses, the pill is winning the wrong battle). Roll back if simulator_page_first_run_completion_rate_from_bikes_referrer drops >15% vs. the site-wide baseline (pill may be recruiting low-intent curiosity clicks that bounce off the simulator) or if bikes_page_bounce_rate rises >10% (visual noise reads as cluttered/spammy). No decision before 200 samples per arm. If B wins, evaluate: (a) adding a /simulator?bike=<id> deeplink as a SEPARATE follow-up experiment to test pre-selection vs. the simulator's own EXP-003 default, (b) replicating the pattern on /bikes/<id> detail pages (one prominent CTA above the spec sheet).

experiments.element: inline mid-article 'Run this comparison' CTA card injected after the stock-sim numbers table
experiments.hypothesis: Mid-article readers on the Pulsar NS200 vs Apache RTR 200 4V comparison post reach the stock-sim numbers table (~1/3 down the page) at peak comparison intent — they have just absorbed the spec sheet and the simulator's ET prediction for both bikes and are in the most likely 'let me check this myself' mental state of the entire read. The current page has exactly ONE simulator CTA: a card at the bottom of the article (line 316, post-conclusion, just above 'Related reading'). By the time readers reach that CTA, most have either bounced from the article or scrolled past the conclusion into the related-reading link block. An inline CTA card injected at the intent peak — i.e. immediately after the stock-sim numbers table, not at the end of the funnel — should lift simulator_runs/blog_post_visitor without affecting scroll depth, time-on-page, or SEO. The two CTAs target different reader cohorts (mid-article scanners vs full-read finishers), so cannibalisation of the end-of-post CTA should be minimal. Distinct from EXP-004 (different blog post: /blog/the-physics-of-a-perfect-launch, with a different intent profile — physics-deep-dive readers vs Indian-market comparison-shoppers) and EXP-006 (blog INDEX, not a post). This is the first post-level intent-peak CTA test.
experiments.variant_a: control: only the existing end-of-post CTA card (line 316) is rendered. No mid-article simulator affordance.
experiments.variant_b: an inline glass-card CTA is rendered immediately after the stock-sim numbers table, with copy 'Want to test this on your own bike?' + 'Run this comparison →' button linking to /simulator. End-of-post CTA is preserved unchanged on both arms.
experiments.implementation_notes: useSearchParams() lives inside InlineSimCtaInner in web/app/blog/pulsar-ns200-vs-apache-rtr-200-quarter-mile-physics/InlineSimCta.js, wrapped in <Suspense fallback={null}> per the App-Router static-prerender / CSR-bailout rule documented in CLAUDE.md. The Suspense fallback is null, so the SSR/SSG output for both arms is byte-identical to the pre-EXP-010 page — zero layout shift, zero hydration mismatch, zero SEO drift on the control. Implementation pattern: the post's CONTENT array gained a single sentinel block { type: 'inline-cta' } placed immediately after the stock-sim numbers table; the Prose renderer dispatches this type to <InlineSimCta />, which is the client component above. Server component / client component boundary kept clean: page.js stays a server component, only InlineSimCta.js is 'use client'. Meta tags (title, description, canonical, openGraph, structured data) are unchanged across arms. data-exp='EXP-010' + data-variant + data-cta='blog-inline-mid-article' + data-post on the CTA so click-attribution survives without analytics infra. No page conflict with EXP-001..009 — the /blog/pulsar-ns200-vs-apache-rtr-200-quarter-mile-physics post had zero live experiments. EXP-004 owns a different blog post (physics-of-a-perfect-launch); EXP-006 owns the /blog INDEX. The end-of-post CTA card at line ~316 is intentionally untouched so the experiment isolates the inline mid-article CTA as the single variable.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator_runs/blog_post_visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND blog_end_of_post_cta_click_through_rate does not drop >25% (the end-of-post CTA serves a different cohort — deep readers — and should retain most of its conversion). Roll back if post_scroll_depth_p50 drops >15% (mid-article CTA reads as interruption rather than affordance, pushing readers to bounce instead of continue), or if simulator_page_first_run_completion_rate from the post referrer drops >15% vs. site-wide baseline (CTA is recruiting low-intent curiosity clicks). Hold for ≥200 samples per arm before declaring either outcome. If B wins: (a) replicate the pattern on the other 28 blog posts at the same structural location (post-stock-sim-table / post-headline-numbers block); (b) consider promoting the variant to a shared <InlineSimCta /> component in web/components/blog/ for reuse rather than per-post duplication.

experiments.element: top-right 'Simulate this bike' CTA copy beside the bike title
experiments.hypothesis: Visitors who reach a bike-detail page (/bikes/<id>) are at peak intent — they have already filtered the 754-bike catalog down to one specific bike, scrolled into its detail page, and are reading specs to answer the implicit question 'how fast is THIS bike?'. The current top CTA copy 'Simulate this bike →' describes the mechanism (open a sim) rather than the outcome (the visitor will learn the bike's quarter-mile ET). Variant B replaces the button label with 'See its quarter-mile ET →' — names the concrete output the visitor came for, on the click target itself. If verb-result framing reduces the moment-of-click hesitation, bike-detail → simulator CTR (and downstream simulator-runs/bike-detail-visitor) should rise. Distinct from EXP-001 (landing-hero, cold visitor), EXP-008 (features mid-funnel), and EXP-009 (/bikes catalog grid, browse mode) — this is a high-intent single-bike-locked-in cohort. EXP-009's decision-criteria block explicitly suggested replicating the catalog pattern onto /bikes/<id> detail pages as a SEPARATE follow-up; EXP-011 picks up that thread but tests COPY on the existing top CTA rather than adding a new affordance (single-variable rule).

Only the button label text changes across arms; the href (/simulator?bike_id=<id>), Gauge icon, Tailwind classes, and the bottom CTA card pair (Simulate this bike / Back to catalog at lines 217-230 of page.js) are unchanged on both arms. Note potential funnel interaction with EXP-009 (a visitor at /bikes?variant=B clicks the Run-sim pill → goes to /simulator directly, never sees EXP-011; a visitor at /bikes?variant=B who instead clicks a card → arrives at /bikes/<id>?variant=B → sees EXP-011 B). Segment funnel attribution by referrer arm before declaring EXP-011 lift.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/bike-detail-visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND bike_detail_bottom_cta_click_through_rate does not increase >20% in absolute terms (we want the top CTA copy to win on its own merits, not shift clicks downward to the bottom card — if the lift is entirely redistributed to the bottom CTA we have not actually improved the page, the visitor simply scrolled).
